title: Billing Rulebook Clause on Service Credit Settlement for Workplace Cafe Management Program Contracts
content:
Where contracted meal periods were not served, the client is credited for them, and the credit is allowed rather than paid out. The credit is allowed against the management fee invoice most recently raised on the contract and is quoted against the billing period that invoice covers, whatever periods the claims behind it concern.

**The quantities the credit is built from**

The claim days counted are the service credit claims standing approved on the contract over the standard claim window, being the 3 months up to the day the credit is worked out, read from the service request log of the workplace cafe management contract held under the Workplace Cafe Management Program. No claim day is set aside, so the claim days set aside are 0, and the net claim days are the claim days counted. Each net claim day is credited as one meal period, so the credited meal periods are the net claim days. Each credited meal period earns the credit rate printed against the service model in force applied to the fee base, which is the monthly management fee printed against that service model.

**How the figures assemble**

The credit for one meal period is the fee base taken at the credit rate and rounded to the nearest cent. The credit worked out is that figure multiplied by the credited meal periods and rounded to the nearest cent. The credit allowed is the lesser of the credit worked out and the billing period ceiling, which is the monthly management fee printed against the service model in force taken at the service credit ceiling printed against that same service model.

| Quantity | Where it is read or how it is struck |
| --- | --- |
| claim days counted | service credit claims standing approved on the contract over the 3 months up to the day the credit is worked out |
| claim days set aside | 0 |
| net claim days | the claim days counted |
| credited meal periods | one meal period for each net claim day |
| credit rate | the rate printed against the service model in force |
| fee base | the monthly management fee printed against that service model |
| credit for one meal period | the fee base taken at the credit rate, rounded to the nearest cent |
| credit worked out | the credit for one meal period multiplied by the credited meal periods, rounded to the nearest cent |
| billing period ceiling | the monthly management fee printed against the service model in force taken at the service credit ceiling printed against that same service model |
| credit allowed | the lesser of the credit worked out and the billing period ceiling |

**Worked through on hypothetical inputs**

Take a contract hypothetically carrying a monthly management fee of 6000.00 USD for its service model, a credit rate of 3.75 per cent printed against that model and a service credit ceiling of 18.00 per cent printed against the same model, with 4 service credit claims standing approved over the 3 months up to the day the credit is worked out. The claim days counted are 4 and the net claim days are 4, so the credited meal periods are 4. The fee base is 6000.00 USD. The credit for one meal period is 6000.00 USD taken at 3.75 per cent, 225.00 USD, rounded to the nearest cent. The credit worked out is 225.00 USD multiplied by 4, 900.00 USD, rounded to the nearest cent. The billing period ceiling is 6000.00 USD taken at 18.00 per cent, 1080.00 USD. The credit allowed is the lesser of 900.00 USD and 1080.00 USD, that is 900.00 USD.

On the same hypothetical figures with 12 approved claim days over those 3 months, the credited meal periods are 12 and the credit worked out is 2700.00 USD; the billing period ceiling remains 1080.00 USD, so the credit allowed is 1080.00 USD. Where the credit worked out and the billing period ceiling stand at the same figure, that figure is the credit allowed.
